findings.description: `inertFences` now runs `.replace(/<(?=[a-z])/gi, "<​")` over the whole body, inside code spans and fences too, breaking the `<https://...>` permalink every important body carries, adding U+200B to quoted code such as `Array<string>`, and turning legitimate HTML into literal text; the comment's claim that the text "reads as it did" is false.
findings.body:
**This rewrite breaks the permalink every important comment carries, and changes quoted code.**

`inertFences` now adds a zero-width space after every `<` followed by a letter. It does this everywhere in the body, code included:

```ts
    .replace(/<(?=[a-z])/gi, "<​");
```

- The review skill (§8, `.claude/skills/pr-ci-review/SKILL.md:152`) tells every `important` body to cite its code as `<https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/blob/SHA/path#La-Lb>`. That becomes `<​https://...>`, which is no longer a CommonMark autolink, so the brackets render as literal text. If GFM's bare-URL autolink picks the link up, it probably keeps the trailing `>`, so no line range gets highlighted. Every line comment the poster sends goes through `commentBody` (`post-review.script.ts:87`), so all of them are affected.
- Code quoted in fences or spans (`Array<string>`, `Map<K, V>`, `#include <stdio.h>`, JSX `<div>`) looks unchanged but now contains U+200B. Copying it out gives an "invalid character" compile error that the reader can't see.
- Legitimate HTML in a body (`<details>`, `<sub>`, `<kbd>`) renders as literal text.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/8678d9c0a733f4388fe37092edf009f44435d5bc/tools/review/src/review-body.utils.ts#L30-L45

The only tag this has to defuse is `<pre`. A tag name must directly follow `<`, so you can neutralise every `<pre` opener without working out where the tag ends. That still covers the code-span, blockquote and NBSP cases, and it leaves every other `<` alone. All five raw-tag rows in the "makes … inert" table still pass. When you make the change, reword lines 30-32 to say that only a `<pre` opener is broken, and add a "leaves as written" row for a body that holds a `<https://...>` permalink and a quoted `Array<string>`.

findings.description: The relocation prefix `Re: \`${finding.file}:${relocatedFrom}\`` skips `inertFences`, so a path containing a backtick and `<pre lang="suggestion">` could render a committable block on a relocated comment. Only the PR author controls that path, though, so this gives no escalation. Wrapping the prefix in `inertFences(...)` closes it.

The new `inertFences` comment names only `<pre lang="suggestion">` while the rewrite touches every `<` before a letter, and the clause "where a tag ends inside markdown only a full parser knows, so no tag opens at all" is a hard-to-parse comma splice.

The new test comment "A lazy footnote label backtracks exponentially…" restates the source comment at `review-body.utils.ts:36-37` and sits above a test this commit otherwise leaves untouched. Delete it, or cut it down to why the test uses 28 labels.

process_issues.description: The validator's `git diff 799fa48..HEAD`, `git show HEAD` and `git show 799fa48:<path>` calls were blocked as needing approval, so it fell back to `gh pr diff` and the checked-out tree. The verdict did not depend on the base comparison.

The `.claude/rules` injection for the conventions reviewer contained only the `@docs/conventions/*.md` loader lines, not the doc bodies, so the reviewer used Grep on docs/conventions to read the rule text.
